The U.S. HVAC industry is in the middle of a generational transition: heat-pump adoption, the R-410A phase-down, and extreme-weather demand are all reshaping the market simultaneously. Operators who modernize quickly are positioned to take share.

Key industry insights

Heat Pump Surge

Residential heat-pump installs grew 25%+ YoY in 2024, driven by IRA tax credits and rising gas prices.

Refrigerant Transition

R-410A phase-down accelerates through 2026–2027; A2L refrigerants change training, parts, and pricing.

Service-Plan Economics

Recurring maintenance contracts are the highest-margin line and drive 2.4x customer lifetime value.

Talent Pipeline

Apprenticeship and EPA-certification programs are the top constraint on crew expansion in 78% of metros.

Competitive landscape

The industry is fragmented, with thousands of small businesses and a mix of regional and national players.

Methodology & sources

Sherlock Research reports combine national datasets with local survey data and proprietary modeling. Every figure is labelled with its sample size, data vintage, and geographic coverage. Primary sources include the U.S. Census Bureau, the Bureau of Labor Statistics, trade-association reports, and Sherlock consumer panels and operator interviews.

Questions before you buy.

What's the difference between the four options?

Standard ($497) is the full national report. City-Specific ($597) adds a local data cut for the metro you choose. Quarterly + Coaching ($2,000/yr) keeps one industry current all year with four updates and four 1:1 calls. All-Access ($2,997, one-time) unlocks every industry report we publish — best if you operate or invest across multiple verticals. For comparison, a single IBISWorld seat runs around $8,000 per year.

Which metros are available for the City-Specific report?

We currently cover 22 U.S. metros: Atlanta, Austin, Boston, Charlotte, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Detroit, Houston, Los Angeles, Miami, Minneapolis, New York, Philadelphia, Phoenix, Riverside, San Antonio, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle, Tampa, and Washington. If your exact market isn't listed, we'll build the local cut for you within 48 hours at no extra cost.

Can I upgrade later?

Yes. Any one-time purchase credits toward an upgrade within 30 days. Most buyers start with a single report, then move to Quarterly once they see the value of ongoing data and coaching.

How current is the data?

The 2026 edition reflects the latest available data, refreshed in May 2026. Quarterly subscribers receive an updated edition every quarter, plus a coaching call to apply it.

Is this a download or a subscription?

Standard, City-Specific, and All-Access are instant PDF downloads, yours to keep and use within your business. Quarterly + Coaching is an annual subscription that includes the downloads plus updates and calls.
